title: User roles and permissions
reading_md:
## What it is

GA4 has five standard roles, listed from most to least access:

| Role | What it can do |
|---|---|
| Administrator | Full control, including managing users |
| Editor | Change settings, but not manage users |
| Marketer | Marketing settings: audiences, key events, attribution and event settings |
| Analyst | Create and share explorations and other shared assets |
| Viewer | View data only |

Roles can be given at account level or at property level. **Data restrictions**, "No cost metrics" and "No revenue metrics", hide those metrics from a user, on top of the role.

Tasks from other lessons, with the lowest role that can do each one:

| Task | Lowest role |
|---|---|
| Add or remove users | Administrator |
| Create a Google Ads link | Editor |
| Change the reporting identity | Editor |
| Set up cross-domain measurement or custom channel groups | Editor |
| Change the report Library | Editor |
| Create audiences or mark key events | Marketer |
| Import key events into Google Ads as conversions | Marketer |
| Create and share explorations | Analyst |
| Read reports | Viewer |

## What the exam asks

Choosing the least-privilege role for a scenario: the lowest role that can do the job, and no more. Voltmarkt examples:

- The pricing team builds explorations and shares them with each other: Analyst.
- Store managers only read reports: Viewer.
- The web developer changes data stream settings but should not manage users: Editor.

## Common confusions

- Analyst is not Viewer: an Analyst can create and share explorations.
- Marketer sits between Analyst and Editor.
- Only an Administrator manages users. An Editor cannot.
- Hiding revenue or cost is a data restriction added to a role, not a role of its own.
- A data restriction limits what one user sees. A data filter changes the property's data itself.

## In Skillshop

Course "Google Analytics Certification (2026)": privacy and administration topics are spread over the modules "Get Started Using Google Analytics" and "Use GA with Other Tools and Data Sources" (Unverified).
